extra_vocab.en: a round sandwich with a meat patty inside
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於餐廳、員工餐廳與菜單的情境，口語常縮寫成 burger；也常和 fries（薯條）、drink 組成套餐。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: hamburger 是可數名詞：a hamburger、two hamburgers；指「牛絞肉」時才是不可數（美式用法）。

example.en: The shop sells about two hundred hamburgers every day.
example.zh: 這家店每天大約賣出兩百個漢堡。

example.en: I would like to order a hamburger and a cola.
example.zh: 我想點一個漢堡和一杯可樂。

example.en: The new hamburger restaurant opens near the station next week.
example.zh: 新的漢堡餐廳下週會在車站附近開幕。

example.en: The set meal comes with a hamburger and fries.
example.zh: 這份套餐附有漢堡和薯條。

examples.en: She ordered a hamburger and a cold drink for lunch.
examples.zh: 她午餐點了一個漢堡和一杯冷飲。

examples.en: The cafeteria sells a hamburger for only five dollars.
examples.zh: 員工餐廳的漢堡只賣五美元。

examples.en: Our menu offers a chicken hamburger for customers who avoid beef.
examples.zh: 我們的菜單為不吃牛肉的顧客提供雞肉漢堡。

similar.diff: burger 是 hamburger 的口語簡稱，菜單與日常對話中更常見。

example.en: The cheese burger is our most popular item on the menu.
example.zh: 起司漢堡是我們菜單上最受歡迎的品項。

similar.diff: sandwich 泛指兩片麵包夾餡料；hamburger 專指夾肉排的圓麵包。

example.en: He ate a sandwich at his desk during lunch.
example.zh: 他午餐時在辦公桌前吃了一個三明治。

example.en: Please look at the menu before you order.
example.zh: 點餐前請先看看菜單。

example.en: The cafeteria is open from noon to two.
example.zh: 員工餐廳的營業時間是中午到兩點。

senses.en: a sandwich made with a round piece of beef

example.en: I usually get a hamburger from the shop near my office.
example.zh: 我通常在公司附近的店買漢堡。

senses.en: beef that has been cut into very small pieces
senses.distinguish: 出現在食譜或採購清單，前面接重量單位時，指的是絞肉而不是漢堡。

example.en: The recipe calls for one pound of hamburger.
example.zh: 這份食譜需要一磅牛絞肉。

extra_vocab.en: a person who owns the house or apartment where they live
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於房貸、保險、房屋維修與社區公告的情境，指擁有並住在自己房子裡的人。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 常見的 homeowners association（社區管理委員會）中的 homeowners 不加所有格 's；指個人要寫 a homeowner。

example.en: Many homeowners called the bank about the new interest rate.
example.zh: 許多屋主打電話到銀行詢問新的利率。

example.en: Homeowners insurance covers damage from fire and storms.
example.zh: 屋主保險涵蓋火災與暴風雨造成的損失。

example.en: The bank offers a special loan for first-time homeowners.
example.zh: 銀行為首次購屋者提供特別貸款。

example.en: The homeowners association meets on the first Monday of each month.
example.zh: 社區管理委員會每個月第一個週一開會。

examples.en: The homeowner asked a contractor to repair the roof.
examples.zh: 屋主請承包商修理屋頂。

examples.en: A homeowner must pay property tax every year.
examples.zh: 屋主每年都必須繳納房屋稅。

examples.en: Our company helps homeowners save money on energy bills.
examples.zh: 我們公司幫助屋主節省能源費用。

confusable.diff: landlord 是把房子出租給別人的房東；homeowner 是擁有並自己住在房子裡的人。

example.en: The landlord raised the rent for the apartment this month.
example.zh: 房東這個月調漲了公寓的租金。

example.en: The tenant must pay the rent by the fifth.
example.zh: 房客必須在五號前繳納租金。

example.en: They pay their mortgage on the first day of the month.
example.zh: 他們每個月一號繳房貸。

derived.link: 最基礎的字，homeowner 是 home（家）+ owner（擁有者）合在一起

extra_vocab.en: a small book that gives rules or useful information
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於新進員工說明、公司規定與產品使用的情境，最常見的是 employee handbook（員工手冊）。

example.en: We printed five hundred handbooks for the new employees.
example.zh: 我們為新進員工印了五百本手冊。

example.en: The employee handbook explains our rules about vacation days.
example.zh: 員工手冊說明了我們關於休假日的規定。

example.en: Please read the user handbook before you start the machine.
example.zh: 啟動機器之前請先閱讀使用手冊。

example.en: The student handbook lists the rules for the library.
example.zh: 學生手冊列出了圖書館的規定。

examples.en: Every new hire will receive a handbook on the first day.
examples.zh: 每位新進員工第一天都會拿到一本手冊。

examples.en: The updated handbook is attached to this email for your review.
examples.zh: 更新後的手冊附在這封郵件中供您參閱。

examples.en: You can find the safety rules in the company handbook.
examples.zh: 你可以在公司手冊中找到安全規定。

confusable.diff: handout 是會議或課堂上發的講義、資料；handbook 是可以長期參考的手冊。

example.en: I gave each person a handout at the start of the meeting.
example.zh: 會議一開始，我給每個人發了一份講義。

similar.diff: manual 多指機器或軟體的操作說明書；handbook 範圍較廣，也包含規定與制度。

example.en: The manual shows how to repair the printer step by step.
example.zh: 說明書逐步說明如何修理印表機。

similar.diff: guide 是指引或導覽，較簡短；handbook 內容較完整、像一本小書。

example.en: This quick guide explains how to book a meeting room.
example.zh: 這份簡易指南說明如何預約會議室。

example.en: The leave policy is explained on page ten.
example.zh: 請假規定在第十頁有說明。

example.en: Please follow the guidelines when you write the report.
example.zh: 撰寫報告時請遵守指導方針。

extra_vocab.en: a device you wear over your ears to listen to sound
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於辦公設備、採購與產品介紹的情境，通常用複數 headphones，一副耳機要說 a pair of headphones。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 指耳機時通常用複數 headphones；一副耳機說 a pair of headphones，動詞用複數（The headphones are...）。單數 headphone 多見於 headphone jack 等搭配。

example.en: Please return the headphones to the front desk after use.
example.zh: 使用後請把耳機歸還到櫃台。

example.en: Each call center agent receives a pair of headphones.
example.zh: 每位客服中心專員都會領到一副耳機。

example.en: These wireless headphones can last for twenty hours.
example.zh: 這款無線耳機可以使用二十小時。

example.en: Noise-cancelling headphones help me focus in the open office.
example.zh: 抗噪耳機幫助我在開放式辦公室裡專心。

example.en: This laptop has a headphone jack on the left side.
example.zh: 這台筆記型電腦的左側有一個耳機孔。

examples.en: Many staff wear headphones to concentrate on their work.
examples.zh: 許多員工戴耳機來專心工作。

examples.en: We bought twenty headphones for the new call center team.
examples.zh: 我們為新的客服中心團隊買了二十副耳機。

examples.en: The headphones stopped working after only two weeks of use.
examples.zh: 這副耳機只用了兩週就壞了。

confusable.diff: 字尾都是 -phone，但 microphone 是麥克風，用來「收音」；headphone 是耳機，用來「聽」。

example.en: Please speak into the microphone so everyone can hear you.
example.zh: 請對著麥克風說話，讓大家都聽得到。

similar.diff: earphones 是放進耳朵裡的小耳機；headphones 通常是蓋住耳朵的頭戴式耳機。

example.en: He wore earphones while he waited at the airport.
example.zh: 他在機場等候時戴著入耳式耳機。

example.en: The speaker in the meeting room is too quiet.
example.zh: 會議室的喇叭聲音太小了。

example.en: Please turn down the volume during the call.
example.zh: 通話時請把音量調小。

extra_vocab.en: a machine that makes a room or water warm
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於辦公室設備、飯店客房與採購維修的情境，指單一的暖氣設備；整套暖氣系統則多用 heating。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: heater 是可數名詞（a heater、two heaters）；heating 指暖氣系統或供暖，是不可數名詞，不加 s。

example.en: Several heaters in the building are not working properly.
example.zh: 大樓裡有好幾台暖氣機運作不正常。

example.en: Could you turn on the heater in the conference room?
example.zh: 你可以把會議室的暖氣打開嗎？

example.en: An electric heater is safer than a gas one indoors.
example.zh: 在室內使用電暖器比瓦斯暖氣機安全。

example.en: The water heater needs to be replaced before winter.
example.zh: 熱水器需要在冬天前更換。

example.en: Do not leave a space heater on overnight.
example.zh: 請勿讓小型電暖器整晚開著。

examples.en: The office feels cold, so please turn on the heater.
examples.zh: 辦公室覺得很冷，所以請打開暖氣。

examples.en: We need to buy a new heater for the meeting room.
examples.zh: 我們需要為會議室買一台新的暖氣機。

examples.en: The heater stopped working, so we called a repairman.
examples.zh: 暖氣機壞了，所以我們叫了維修人員。

confusable.diff: heating 指整套暖氣系統或供暖；heater 是單一台暖氣設備。
confusable.usage: heating 是不可數名詞（the heating），heater 是可數名詞（a heater）。

example.en: The heating in our building is controlled by a timer.
example.zh: 我們大樓的暖氣系統由定時器控制。

example.en: Please turn off the fan when you leave the room.
example.zh: 離開房間時請關掉電風扇。

example.en: The air conditioner in the lobby is too cold.
example.zh: 大廳的冷氣太冷了。

derived.link: 最基礎的字，heater 是 heat + -er，做事的東西，像 printer、cooler
heat + -ing，把「加熱」這件事變成名詞，像 shop → shopping

extra_vocab.en: a hard hat that protects your head
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於工地、工廠與騎車的安全規定情境，通常和 wear、safety 一起出現，語氣偏規定與提醒。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: wear a helmet 是「戴著安全帽」的狀態，put on a helmet 才是「戴上」的動作。

example.en: Please check that all helmets are stored on the shelf.
example.zh: 請確認所有安全帽都收在架子上。

example.en: Employees must wear a helmet in the loading area.
example.zh: 員工在裝卸區必須戴安全帽。

example.en: A safety helmet protects your head from falling objects.
example.zh: 安全帽可以保護你的頭部不被掉落物打到。

example.en: She always puts on a bicycle helmet before riding.
example.zh: 她騎車前一定會戴上自行車安全帽。

examples.en: All workers must wear a helmet on the construction site.
examples.zh: 所有工人在工地都必須戴安全帽。

examples.en: Delivery riders must wear a helmet while riding.
examples.zh: 外送員騎車時必須戴安全帽。

examples.en: The store sells helmets in many sizes and colors.
examples.zh: 這家店販售多種尺寸與顏色的安全帽。

similar.diff: hard hat 是工地用的硬質安全帽；helmet 範圍較廣，也包含騎車用的頭盔。

example.en: Visitors must wear a hard hat inside the plant.
example.zh: 訪客在廠區內必須戴安全帽。

example.en: Safety training is required for all new staff.
example.zh: 所有新進員工都必須接受安全訓練。

example.en: Staff must wear a clean uniform at work.
example.zh: 員工上班時必須穿乾淨的制服。

extra_vocab.en: one by one, not as a group
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於商品包裝、銷售方式與人事面談的情境，強調「一個一個分開處理」，而不是整批或一起。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: individually 是副詞，常放在過去分詞前（individually wrapped）或動詞後（treated individually）；形容詞是 individual（an individual order）。

example.en: Accessories are sold individually and not included in the set.
example.zh: 配件為單獨販售，不包含在套組內。

example.en: Each cookie is individually wrapped for easy sharing.
example.zh: 每片餅乾都是獨立包裝，方便分享。

example.en: The manager will meet each member individually next week.
example.zh: 經理下週會和每位成員個別面談。

examples.en: Each item is individually packed to prevent damage.
examples.zh: 每件商品都單獨包裝，以避免損壞。

examples.en: The manager talked to each employee individually about goals.
examples.zh: 經理就目標個別和每位員工談話。

examples.en: These batteries can be bought individually or in packs.
examples.zh: 這些電池可以單買，也可以買整包。

confusable.diff: personally 是「親自、就個人而言」；individually 是「一個一個、各自分開」。

example.en: The director personally thanked every member of the team.
example.zh: 主任親自感謝了團隊的每一位成員。

similar.diff: separately 強調「分開處理、不放在一起」；individually 強調「逐一看待每一個」。

example.en: Please pay the two invoices separately this month.
example.zh: 這個月請分開支付這兩張發票。

example.en: The group will visit the factory on Friday.
example.zh: 這個團體週五會參觀工廠。

example.en: Our team finished the project ahead of schedule.
example.zh: 我們的團隊提前完成了專案。

derived.link: 最基礎的字，individual + -ly 變副詞，像 quick → quickly

extra_vocab.en: to fill something with air, or to make a number or price bigger
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於輪胎與氣球等充氣的情境，也常指價格、數字被人為抬高或誇大，帶有負面語氣。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: inflate 是及物動詞，後面要接受詞（inflate a tire）；說「價格被抬高」常用被動：Prices are inflated。通貨膨脹是名詞 inflation。

example.en: A weak currency often inflates the cost of imports.
example.zh: 貨幣疲弱常會推高進口成本。

example.en: The company inflated its profits in the annual report.
example.zh: 公司在年度報告中誇大了利潤。

example.en: Inflated prices made customers buy fewer products last month.
example.zh: 過高的價格讓顧客上個月買得比較少。

example.en: Rising fuel costs are inflating the price of goods.
example.zh: 不斷上漲的燃料成本正在推高商品價格。

example.en: Some stores inflate prices during the holiday season.
example.zh: 有些商店在假期期間哄抬價格。

example.en: We found inflated costs on the supplier's invoice.
example.zh: 我們在供應商的發票上發現了過高的成本。

example.en: He stopped to inflate a tire on the delivery van.
example.zh: 他停下來為送貨車的輪胎充氣。

examples.en: The seller inflated the price to make more profit.
examples.zh: 賣家哄抬價格以賺取更多利潤。

examples.en: Please inflate the tires before the long trip.
examples.zh: 長途旅行前請幫輪胎充氣。

examples.en: The report inflated sales figures to impress the investors.
examples.zh: 這份報告誇大了銷售數字以打動投資人。

confusable.diff: 拼法很像，但 influence 是「影響」，inflate 是「使膨脹、抬高」。
confusable.usage: influence 可當動詞或名詞（influence a decision、a strong influence），inflate 只當動詞。

example.en: The price of oil can influence our shipping costs.
example.zh: 油價可能影響我們的運輸成本。

similar.diff: exaggerate 指把事情說得比實際更嚴重或更好；inflate 常指把數字或價格人為抬高。

example.en: Do not exaggerate the benefits of the new product.
example.zh: 不要誇大新產品的好處。

example.en: The company will raise its prices next month.
example.zh: 公司下個月會調高價格。

example.en: The advertisement seems to exaggerate the size of the room.
example.zh: 這則廣告似乎誇大了房間的大小。

derived.link: inflate 去掉 e + -ion，把「膨脹」變成名詞，像 decorate → decoration
inflate 去掉 e + -able，意思是「可以被充氣的」，像 comfortable

senses.en: to fill something with air or gas

example.en: Staff will inflate the balloons before the guests arrive.
example.zh: 員工會在賓客抵達前把氣球充好氣。

senses.en: to make a price or number higher than it should be
senses.distinguish: 受詞是 price、cost、figures 等數字相關的詞時，指的是人為抬高或誇大。

example.en: Some suppliers inflate their prices when demand is high.
example.zh: 有些供應商在需求高的時候會哄抬價格。
